incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for INC-20260215-42 — high 5xx rate on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 starting ~2026-02-15T03:12Z. Error rate ~12% over 5m, increased fallbacks to smaller model variants. Paging Amber (oncall).

Amber (oncall): on it. I see the bot note. grabbing logs + routing traces. @Ryan can you pull routing-control logs and the policy diffs for the last deploy?

Ryan: ack. pulling routing traces now. initial grep shows a spike in spillover decisions around 03:11:20Z with many routes tagged to `fallback: small-quant` even for enterprise-tier. pasting a tail:

```
2026-02-15T03:11:18Z route_decision user=acct_123 region=eu-west-1 route=primary model=redwood-medium tier=enterprise -> decision=fallback model=redwood-small-qlt reason=capacity_estimate
2026-02-15T03:11:19Z route_decision user=acct_456 region=eu-west-1 route=primary model=redwood-medium tier=enterprise -> decision=fallback model=redwood-small-qlt reason=policy_match
2026-02-15T03:11:20Z route_decision user=acct_789 region=eu-west-1 route=primary model=redwood-large tier=standard -> decision=spillover region=eu-central-1
```

Ryan: full logs attached to the incident bundle (s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20260215-42/routing.log).

Sara: support summary — preliminary customer impact: 4 enterprise customers reported quality regressions (text output truncated or shorter responses), ~1.2k failed requests (500/timeout) and ~3.6k requests routed to lower-quality models in eu-central-1. Flagging account managers.

Maya (ml-ops): quick hypothesis: the failover policy's priority table appears to have an ordering bug — enterprise tier entries were shadowed by a generic fallback entry introduced in last policy PR. I'm seeing a policy blob that looks wrong: 

```
# extracted policy snippet
- match: { tier: enterprise }
  fallback: [redwood-medium, redwood-small-qlt]
- match: { region: eu-west-1 }
  fallback: [redwood-small-qlt]
# intended ordering should prioritize tier match before region fallback
```

Maya (ml-ops): if the region fallback rule evaluates before the tier-specific rule, enterprise traffic would be mapped to small-quant. that would explain quality regressions.

Devon (net-eng): checked infra: no packet loss or host OOMs in eu-west-1. GPU utilization was high but within autoscale thresholds. suggests this is policy/decision layer rather than infra failure.

Amber (oncall): mitigation plan (live):
1) revert routing policy commit that introduced the generic region fallback (assign Ryan)
2) pin enterprise-tier routes to `redwood-medium` for eu-* until we validate (assign Maya)
3) temporary rate-limit/queue non-prod traffic to reduce noisy fanout (assign Devon)
4) prepare customer-facing note (assign Sara/Support Bot)

Ryan: executing revert now. running: `git -C infra-routing revert --no-edit 5f3a2b7` then `./deploy-routing --env=prod --region=eu-west-1 --policy=HEAD~1`

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollback started at 2026-02-15T03:25:33Z for infra-routing (PR 3123).

Ryan: rollback finished 03:27:10Z. routing policy now at commit 5f3a2b6 (pre-change). verifying traffic.

Amber (oncall): monitoring dashboards — errors dropping: 5xx from 12% -> 1.8% within 6m of rollback. quality regression reports down to isolated customers. good sign.

Maya (ml-ops): I've pinned enterprise tiers in a short-circuit mapping to redwood-medium for EU for the next 2 hours while we audit policies: `policy.pin(tier=enterprise, region=eu-*, model=redwood-medium, ttl=2h)` — applied.

Devon (net-eng): applied rate limits for non-prod buckets, no impact to prod telemetry. continuing to watch.

Sara: drafted customer note: "We detected a routing policy regression causing some enterprise requests in EU to hit lower-capacity models; a rollback has been deployed and we're monitoring. We will follow up with RCA and any compensations." pinging AMs.

Support Bot: posted draft to #customer-communications for review.

Amber (oncall): timeline so far:
- 03:11Z spike in policy decisions -> wrong fallback selection
- 03:12Z incident auto-page
- 03:20Z triage + hypothesis (policy ordering)
- 03:25Z rollback initiated
- 03:27Z rollback complete
- 03:33Z metric recovery observed

Maya (ml-ops): collecting policy diffs and PRs. looks like PR 3123 introduced a consolidated fallback rule but missed an explicit `priority` field. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-routing/pull/3123

Ryan: attaching routing decision trace for one affected session: `trace: acct_123 path: primary->fallback(small-qlt) eval_stack: region_rule -> generic_fallback -> applied`

Amber (oncall): immediate post-mortem actions (assigned):
- Maya: produce short RCA note on policy evaluation order + test coverage gaps (due EOD)
- Ryan: add an assertion in CI to prevent region fallback from preempting tier rules (PR open)
- Devon: add a smoke test for spillover path latency thresholds
- Sara/Support Bot: finalize customer comms and send to affected AMs

Maya (ml-ops): working on the RCA doc. preliminary cause: regression in policy evaluation ordering introduced by PR 3123; contributing factor: lack of integration tests around tier vs region fallback precedence.

Amber (oncall): closing the active paging. we'll keep thread pinned for RCA compilation. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: customer note sent to AMs at 03:45Z.

Amber (oncall): follow-ups — schedule a cross-team postmortem session tomorrow 09:30Z, invite: eng-routing, ml-ops, support, net-eng. action owners above.

Ryan: created PR #3180 to add the CI assertion and a unit test for policy ordering.

Maya (ml-ops): uploading policy audit + test plan to the incident folder s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20260215-42/rca/

Amber (oncall): thanks all. We'll add any new findings here.

(incident thread locked for new ephemeral alerts)
